It's easily verifiable (the agent either finds it or doesn't) and can be set up with an interesting scene that requires some navigation. milestones.description: Uses position_near_with_facing because this is a find/locate task. The player must navigate near the birch trapdoor (placed at spawn-relative [5, 2, 7] on the interior west wall of the oak building) and face toward it. max_distance=16 allows detection from a reasonable range while building walls provide natural constraint requiring entry, and facing_tolerance=60 ensures the player is actually looking at the trapdoor to confirm visual identification.

scene_description: A grassy area with two small buildings: an oak planks building (east side, ~5-9 x, ~5-9 z) containing a birch trapdoor on its interior west wall at height 2, and a cobblestone building (west side, ~-6 to ~-3 x, ~5-8 z) with a chest inside. A lantern on stone bricks at (~0, ~0-1, ~4) serves as a central landmark. The player spawns at the center between the two buildings and must explore to find the birch trapdoor inside the oak building.
task_text: Find a birch trapdoor somewhere in the scene. Explore the nearby structures and look inside buildings to locate it.
design_notes: The oak planks building (5x5 footprint) has a 3-wide, 2-tall entrance on its south face (z=5 side). The birch trapdoor is placed on the interior west wall (x=5) at y=2 (eye level), z=7 (middle of the building). When open and facing west, it appears as a visible pale panel contrasting against the darker oak planks. The cobblestone building with chest serves as a distractor to encourage exploration of multiple structures. The lantern on stone bricks provides a central landmark between the buildings. All structures are within ~10 blocks of spawn, keeping the scene compact and navigable.
